payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function, and does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested?

payload.statement: UniProtKB natural variant VAR_072681 at residue 70 (R to W): Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome due to CTLA4 haploinsufficiency; IDAIL. 1 publications cited.
UniProtKB annotates residues 70 of P16410 as Mutagenesis: Strongly reduced interaction with CD80, CD86 and ICOSLG.; evidence: experimental evidence used in manual assertion; PubMed 28484017.

A CD80-expressing cell line transendocytosis flow assay was applied to 24 CTLA4 variants from patients; significantly impaired transendocytosis was shown for 17 variants and seven tested normal; R70W is not named in the retrieved abstract.
gnomAD v4.1: allele 2-203870684-C-T observed 1 times in 1461890 alleles (frequency 6.84e-07; 0 hemizygotes, 0 homozygotes).
A functionally oriented assay measuring CTLA-4 ligand uptake was developed and is described as sensitive to ligand-binding or -trafficking mutations in CTLA-4 pathway genes.
UniProtKB annotates residues 36-161 of P16410 as Topological domain: Extracellular; evidence: curator inference used in manual assertion; PubMed 28484017.

Autosomal dominant loss-of-function CTLA4 variants cause immune dysregulation with incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity, which the authors attribute to a possible role for genetic modifiers (DECTIN-1 identified as a modifier).
UniProtKB annotates residues 39-140 of P16410 as Domain: Ig-like V-type; evidence: imported manually asserted information used in automatic assertion.
UniProtKB annotates residues 68-77 of P16410 as Beta strand; evidence: combinatorial computational and experimental evidence used in automatic assertion.

An in silico pipeline (SIFT, PROVEAN, PolyPhen-2, MutPred2, ConSurf and others) predicted three damaging CTLA4 missense SNPs (rs1553657429, rs1559591863, rs778534474); the abstract does not name R70W and the predictions are not experimentally tested.
AlphaMissense gives p.Arg70Trp of P16410 a AlphaMissense pathogenicity of 0.4657, classed as ambiguous (AlphaMissense class) (scale: 0 to 1; higher = more likely pathogenic).
payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use

The retrieved literature does not show whether R70W behaves as a simple loss of function or as a dominant-negative change when co-expressed with wild-type CTLA-4.
payload.why_it_matters: Whether the mutant protein reduces activity only by lowering the amount of functional protein, or also interferes with the wild-type protein, changes which cell assays would be needed to confirm the loss-of-function mechanism for this exact substitution.

payload.statement: IntAct curates a physical interaction of P16410 with CD80 (8 experiments; MI score 0.88; x-ray crystallography, protein array). The interaction surface is not mapped to residues in this record.
CTLA4 is the gene of the inborn error of immunity 'CTLA4 haploinsufficiency (ALPS-V)' (Diseases of immune dysregulation; Autosomal dominant inheritance).

E4 and E6 give the transendocytosis and ligand-uptake assays that can detect ligand-binding or trafficking loss in CTLA-4, and E8 and E13 give general haploinsufficiency context. E11 is an in silico prediction that does not name R70W. G1-G3 record that the effect of R70W on ligand binding, trafficking, structure and dominant-negative behavior is not established by this literature.

payload.why_it_matters: No assay in the record measures the effect of R70W on function, so the ClinVar and UniProt classifications cannot be checked against a measured functional readout at this residue.

payload.statement: Arg70 sits on the extracellular Ig-V domain at the CD80/CD86 contact surface, and Arg70Trp removes the charged contact and adds a bulky indole, so CTLA-4 binds its ligands weakly and transendocytoses less ligand.
payload.would_refute: Superposing R70W onto the CTLA-4/B7-1 (1I8L) and CTLA-4/B7-2 (1I85) complexes shows residue 70 with no atom within about 4.5 Å of CD80, CD86 or ICOSLG, and the mutant side chain clashes with nothing and loses no contacts.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Only evidence that names this exact residue points here: UniProt records strongly reduced CD80/CD86/ICOSLG interaction for residue 70 (E3). The ALPS-linked pathogenic call (E1, E2) and the transendocytosis assay (E4) fit a ligand-contact loss. Ranked first because it is the only residue-specific functional result. Still missing: the contact map that places residue 70 in the interface (G6), and any direct binding or transendocytosis data for R70W (G1).

payload.statement: Arg70 lies in the Ig-V beta-sheet region (strand 68-77), and the Arg-to-Trp change disturbs local packing or a buried salt bridge, lowering folding stability so that less correctly folded CTLA-4 reaches the cell surface.
payload.would_refute: Residue 70 side chain is solvent-exposed in the 9DQ3, 1I8L and 1I85 structures with no buried salt bridge or hydrogen-bond network partner, and stability predictors (for example FoldX or Rosetta ddG) give R70W a change near zero (|ddG| below about 1 kcal/mol) while the structure-based contact analysis still shows the same ligand contacts as wild type.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Indirect support only. Residue 70 is conserved (E16) and inside a beta strand (E10), and the in-silico scores are mixed: AlphaMissense is ambiguous (E12) and EVE is uncertain (E15), while popEVE is more deleterious (E14). None of these measures folding directly, and no stability data exist for this variant (G1, G2). It ranks below H1 because it is not tied to a residue-specific functional result.

payload.statement: The mutant folds and binds ligand normally but is retained or mistrafficked inside the cell, so less CTLA-4 reaches the surface to engage CD80/CD86 and the ligand-uptake function is reduced.
payload.would_refute: Surface-expression or transendocytosis measurements show R70W at wild-type surface levels and wild-type ligand uptake, or a structure-based check finds residue 70 buried against the core so that the substitution is only a folding defect with no trafficking consequence.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Weakest of the three. It rests on general trafficking sensitivity of the ligand-uptake assay (E6) and on haploinsufficiency with incomplete penetrance (E8, E21) rather than on anything about R70W. No retrieved source tests surface expression for this variant (G1, G4). It is kept as a rival because it can't be excluded yet, and it differs in class from H1 and H2.

payload.summary: Three agent-generated hypotheses are recorded for CTLA4 p.Arg70Trp. H1 (protein_interaction, rank 1): R70W weakens CD80/CD86/ICOSLG binding, favoured by UniProt mutagenesis E3. H2 (stability_folding, rank 2): R70W destabilises the Ig-V strand, supported only indirectly by conservation and mixed predictors. H3 (other, rank 3): R70W causes trafficking retention, which is weakly supported. The next test should superpose R70W on the 1I8L and 1I85 complexes (refutes H1 if no contact is lost) and run a ddG estimate (refutes H2 if |ddG| is near zero).

Insight recorded agent-generated hypotheses H1 (protein interaction, rank 1), H2 (stability/folding, rank 2) and H3 (other, rank 3) for CTLA4 p.Arg70Trp. Plan one single targeted computational test that can discriminate among them within the remaining budget, and state which hypothesis it favours and what result would refute it.

payload.description: FoldX ddG of R70W on the AlphaFold model via ProtVar, with pLDDT at residue 70 and other substitutions at the same residue. A destabilising value (at or above threshold) supports H2 (stability/folding). A neutral value (|ddG| below about 1 kcal/mol) weakens H2 and leaves H1 and H3 unchanged.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: H2 is the only hypothesis whose refutation test (|ddG| below about 1 kcal/mol) is directly measured here, so a neutral result would drop H2 below H1 and H3 while a destabilising result would raise H2 to the top. Both outcomes move H2 in opposite directions. H1 and H3 are not separated by this test, so the ranking moves only partly. The limitation is FoldX error near 1 kcal/mol and a model-based estimate.

Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: P2Rank and ProtVar membership of residue 70 in predicted pockets and predicted protein-protein interfaces on the AlphaFold model. payload.feasibility_reasoning: can_run is true and P2Rank runs on the AlphaFold model, so the pocket part runs. ProtVar interface state is not_covered for this residue, so the interface part may return no data. Cost is 0 compute seconds and 2 tool calls, with no approval needed.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.

payload.description: Contact of residue 70 with organic ligands or metals in the 6 experimental structures that observe the residue and hold a non-solvent ligand. The test only checks soluble analogues bound to CTLA-4, not CD80 or CD86 protein partners.

H1 is a protein-interaction claim about CD80/CD86, and H2 and H3 are about fold and trafficking, so almost any outcome leaves the ranking unchanged. A contact with a small molecule would not confirm H1, and absence would not refute it.

Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.
